items.title: Micron Stock Slips Despite Record Q4, Analyst Price Hikes. Here’s Why MU Stock Is Still a Buy
items.summary: Micron just posted a record quarter, analysts are raising price targets, and the stock still fell. The reason why reveals a deeper tension about where memory markets are actually headed.

items.title: Goldman commits £500m to SME housebuilding lender Quantum
items.summary: Goldman Sachs is committing up to £500m in funding to a specialist SME housebuilding lender in the wake of figures casting fresh doubt on the likelihood of the government achieving its new homes target during this parliament.  Sky News understands that the Wall Street banking giant has agreed to provide the expanded long-term lending facility to Quantum Development Finance - taking its total exposure to the company to as much as £700m.  Founded in 2023, Quantum provides development and bridging finance to SME housebuilders in England and Wales at a time when many of the larger industry players have found their balance sheets under increasing strain.

items.title: Trump Threatens To Ban Diesel Exports To France And Germany Unless They Release 120 Million Barrels From Reserves. Analysts Say Ban Could Backfire On American Drivers.
items.summary: Washington is threatening to cut off diesel exports to France and Germany unless they drain 120 million barrels from emergency reserves, but the official wielding that threat already said the tool is broken.

items.title: Bank Stocks Are Beaten Down. The Case for Buying Now.
items.summary: The outlook for bank stocks can’t get much worse, and that’s exactly why they look appealing.  The  ETF, home to investment banks and other lenders, has fallen 12% to $63 from an August record high of just over $71.  One reason for those worries is the Federal Reserve’s September interest-rate increase.

items.title: Goldman pushes Fed rate hike to December after cooler inflation
items.summary: Investing.com -- Goldman Sachs has pushed back its forecast for the next Federal Reserve rate hike from October to December following a softer-than-expected August inflation reading, while warning that the tightening cycle may already be over.
